sections.title: Physical properties of organic compounds

questions.q: Define the term boiling point.
questions.qAf: Definieer die term kookpunt.
points: The temperature at which the vapour pressure of a liquid
pointsAf: Die temperatuur waarby die dampdruk van ’n vloeistof
gelyk is aan die atmosferiese (eksterne) druk

questions.q: Why were compounds with similar molar masses chosen for this comparison?
questions.qAf: Waarom is verbindings met soortgelyke molêre massas vir hierdie vergelyking gekies?
points: So that the London forces are about the same and only the functional group affects the boiling point (fair test)
pointsAf: Sodat die London-kragte omtrent dieselfde is en net die funksionele groep die kookpunt beïnvloed (regverdige toets)

questions.q: Explain the difference between the boiling points of ethanal and ethanol. Refer to the type and strength of the intermolecular forces.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik die verskil tussen die kookpunte van etanaal en etanol. Verwys na die soort en sterkte van die intermolekulêre kragte.
points: Ethanal has dipole-dipole forces (and London forces) between its molecules
ethanol has hydrogen bonds between its molecules
hydrogen bonds are stronger than dipole-dipole forces
so more energy is needed to overcome the forces in ethanol
pointsAf: Etanaal het dipool-dipoolkragte (en London-kragte) tussen sy molekules
etanol het waterstofbindings tussen sy molekules
dus is meer energie nodig om die kragte in etanol te oorkom

questions.q: Which compound in the table has the highest vapour pressure at room temperature? Give a reason.
questions.qAf: Watter verbinding in die tabel het die hoogste dampdruk by kamertemperatuur? Gee ’n rede.
points: it has only weak London forces between its molecules (the weakest intermolecular forces)
pointsAf: dit het net swak London-kragte tussen sy molekules (die swakste intermolekulêre kragte)

questions.q: Explain why methanoic acid has a higher boiling point than ethanol.
questions.qAf: Verduidelik waarom metanoësuur ’n hoër kookpunt as etanol het.
points: Methanoic acid has two sites for hydrogen bonding (forms dimers)
so its intermolecular forces are stronger and more energy is needed to overcome them
pointsAf: Metanoësuur het twee plekke vir waterstofbinding (vorm dimere)
dus is sy intermolekulêre kragte sterker en is meer energie nodig om hulle te oorkom

questions.q: Which has the higher boiling point: butane or 2-methylpropane? Give a reason.
questions.qAf: Watter een het die hoër kookpunt: butaan of 2-metielpropaan? Gee ’n rede.
points: butane: it is unbranched, has a larger contact surface and so stronger London forces
pointsAf: butaan: dit is onvertak, het ’n groter kontakoppervlak en dus sterker London-kragte

sections.intro:
Study the reactions below.
Reaction 1: ethene + HCl → chloroethane
Reaction 2: chloroethane + dilute NaOH (mild heat) → ethanol
Reaction 3: ethanol + concentrated H₂SO₄ (heat) → ethene + water
Reaction 4: ethanol + ethanoic acid (concentrated H₂SO₄, heat) → ester + water
sections.introAf:
Bestudeer die reaksies hieronder.
Reaksie 1: eteen + HCl → chloroetaan
Reaksie 2: chloroetaan + verdunde NaOH (matige hitte) → etanol
Reaksie 3: etanol + gekonsentreerde H₂SO₄ (hitte) → eteen + water
Reaksie 4: etanol + etanoësuur (gekonsentreerde H₂SO₄, hitte) → ester + water

sections.title: Rate of reaction

questions.q: Define reaction rate.
questions.qAf: Definieer reaksietempo.
points: The change in concentration (amount/mass/volume) of reactants or products
pointsAf: Die verandering in konsentrasie (hoeveelheid/massa/volume) van reaktante of produkte

questions.q: Write down the independent variable in this investigation.
questions.qAf: Skryf die onafhanklike veranderlike in hierdie ondersoek neer.

questions.q: Use the collision theory to explain why the reaction in experiment II is faster.
questions.qAf: Gebruik die botsingsteorie om te verduidelik waarom die reaksie in eksperiment II vinniger is.
points: At a higher temperature the particles have more kinetic energy
more particles have energy equal to or greater than the activation energy
so there are more effective collisions per unit time
pointsAf: By ’n hoër temperatuur het die deeltjies meer kinetiese energie
meer deeltjies het energie gelyk aan of groter as die aktiveringsenergie
dus is daar meer effektiewe botsings per eenheidtyd

questions.q: Show by calculation that the hydrochloric acid is in excess.
questions.qAf: Toon deur berekening dat die soutsuur in oormaat is.
points: n(HCl) available = 1,5 × 0,2 = 0,3 mol > 0,2 mol, so HCl is in excess
pointsAf: n(HCl) beskikbaar = 1,5 × 0,2 = 0,3 mol > 0,2 mol, dus is HCl in oormaat

questions.q: Experiment II is complete after 120 s. Calculate the average rate of hydrogen production in dm³·s⁻¹.
questions.qAf: Eksperiment II is ná 120 s voltooi. Bereken die gemiddelde tempo van waterstofproduksie in dm³·s⁻¹.

questions.q: A small amount of copper(II) sulfate acts as a catalyst for this reaction. Explain how a catalyst increases the reaction rate.
questions.qAf: ’n Klein hoeveelheid koper(II)sulfaat dien as katalisator vir hierdie reaksie. Verduidelik hoe ’n katalisator die reaksietempo verhoog.
points: It provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
so more particles have enough energy and there are more effective collisions per unit time
pointsAf: Dit verskaf ’n alternatiewe pad met ’n laer aktiveringsenergie
dus het meer deeltjies genoeg energie en is daar meer effektiewe botsings per eenheidtyd

sections.intro:
Learners add 6,5 g of zinc granules to 200 cm³ of hydrochloric acid of concentration 1,5 mol·dm⁻³:
Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) → ZnCl₂(aq) + H₂(g)
Experiment I is done at 25 °C and experiment II at 40 °C. All other conditions are the same.
sections.introAf:
Leerders voeg 6,5 g sinkkorrels by 200 cm³ soutsuur met ’n konsentrasie van 1,5 mol·dm⁻³:
Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) → ZnCl₂(aq) + H₂(g)
Eksperiment I word by 25 °C gedoen en eksperiment II by 40 °C. Alle ander toestande is dieselfde.

sections.title: Chemical equilibrium

questions.q: What is meant by a dynamic equilibrium?
questions.qAf: Wat word met ’n dinamiese ewewig bedoel?
points: The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction
so the concentrations of the reactants and products stay constant
pointsAf: Die tempo van die voorwaartse reaksie is gelyk aan die tempo van die terugwaartse reaksie
dus bly die konsentrasies van die reaktante en produkte konstant

questions.q: Calculate the equilibrium constant K_c at temperature T.
questions.qAf: Bereken die ewewigskonstante K_c by temperatuur T.

questions.q: The temperature is increased. Will the value of K_c INCREASE, DECREASE or STAY THE SAME? Explain.
questions.qAf: Die temperatuur word verhoog. Sal die waarde van K_c TOENEEM, AFNEEM of DIESELFDE BLY? Verduidelik.
points: the forward reaction is endothermic, so it is favoured
pointsAf: die voorwaartse reaksie is endotermies, dus word dit bevoordeel

questions.q: The volume of the container is decreased at constant temperature. How will this affect the amount of NO₂ at equilibrium? Explain.
questions.qAf: Die volume van die houer word by konstante temperatuur verklein. Hoe sal dit die hoeveelheid NO₂ by ewewig beïnvloed? Verduidelik.
points: the pressure increases, so the reaction that produces fewer moles of gas is favoured
the reverse reaction (2 mol gas on the right, 1 mol on the left)
pointsAf: die druk neem toe, dus word die reaksie wat minder mol gas lewer, bevoordeel
die terugwaartse reaksie (2 mol gas regs, 1 mol links)

questions.q: A catalyst is added to the system at equilibrium. How does this affect the amount of NO₂? Explain.
questions.qAf: ’n Katalisator word by die stelsel in ewewig gevoeg. Hoe beïnvloed dit die hoeveelheid NO₂? Verduidelik.
points: a catalyst increases the rates of the forward and reverse reactions equally
pointsAf: ’n katalisator verhoog die tempo’s van die voorwaartse en terugwaartse reaksies ewe veel

sections.intro:
0,6 mol N₂O₄(g) is sealed in an empty 2 dm³ container at temperature T. The reaction reaches equilibrium:
N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) ΔH > 0
At equilibrium the container holds 0,4 mol NO₂(g).
sections.introAf:
0,6 mol N₂O₄(g) word in ’n leë houer van 2 dm³ by temperatuur T verseël. Die reaksie bereik ewewig:
N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) ΔH > 0
By ewewig bevat die houer 0,4 mol NO₂(g).

in chemiese energie omgesit word (’n nie-spontane reaksie word deur elektrisiteit aangedryf)
